automation.heroSub: I automate them — in weeks, not months. No big project, no system swap, measurable ROI from month one.
automation.problem1Text: Delivery notes, orders and invoices are entered into the ERP by hand.
automation.problem2Text: Order confirmations, follow-ups and status queries live in email — and get stuck there.
automation.problem3Text: Quality documents, inspection reports and minutes are produced and filed by hand.
automation.problemFooter: These are not IT problems. These are process problems, solvable with the right tools.
automation.step1Desc: Half a day on site. I look at where the manual bridges are and identify the process with the biggest lever.
automation.step2Desc: In 1–2 weeks I build a working prototype. You test it with real data and give feedback.
automation.step3Desc: After tweaks the automation goes to production. Includes 30 days of support.
automation.aboutMiniText: Computer-science degree at UZH, professional experience at UBS and KPMG, club president for 200 members. I understand both the technology and the everyday life of organisations.
automation.bottomCtaHeading: Let's spend 20 minutes finding out which process gives you the most leverage.

network.title: Network
network.subtitle: Inbound traffic through Cloudflare, source-IP reputation, firewall events, LAN access to the cluster nodes and egress from cluster workloads. Data from data-service, loaded fresh on every page view.
network.disabled: data-service not configured in this environment (DATA_SERVICE_URL unset).
network.malformed: Unexpected response from data-service — no data shown.

status.title: Collectors
status.failures: {count, plural, one {# consecutive failure} other {# consecutive failures}}

ip.title: IP detail
ip.notFound: This IP was not seen in the window.

lan.title: LAN (cluster nodes)
lan.subtitle: Connections, firewall blocks and SSH logins at the four cluster nodes, from each node's conntrack table and journal.
lan.connectionsNote: Peak concurrent TCP connections per 15-minute window, by source and conntrack state.
lan.ufwNote: UFW rate-limits its log, so these counts are a lower bound.
lan.fromListedRows: {count, plural, one {Derived from the # listed row.} other {Derived from the # listed rows.}}
lan.sshNote: Failed counts failed authentication for existing users and is a lower bound: sshd logs rejected keys only when a connection gives up. Unknown usernames count as invalid user. SSH through the Cloudflare tunnel shows up as a pod or node address, not the real client.
lan.noDataYet: No LAN data yet: the node collector has not reported. Data appears about 30 minutes after the netmon_node role is rolled out to the nodes.

egress.title: Egress
egress.subtitle: Outbound TCP connections from cluster workloads to external destinations, from the coroot node agent's per-container counters. Hourly aggregates; FQDNs come from DNS answers the agent observed.
egress.newHint: Not seen for this workload and destination in the previous 30 days.
egress.fromListedRows: {count, plural, one {Totals derived from the # listed flow (top flows by traffic).} other {Totals derived from the # listed flows (top flows by traffic).}}
egress.note: A destination's first hour can be undercounted: the counters only start when the agent first sees the connection.
egress.noDataYet: No egress data yet: the egress collector has not succeeded. Data appears about an hour after the coroot node agent runs on the nodes.
egress.emptyHint: If this stays empty, check that the coroot node agent runs on the nodes.
egress.disabledHint: The egress collector is disabled in data-service.
